items.title: Husband forcing wife to accept extramarital affair and live with mistress is mental cruelty: Jharkhand High Court
items.summary: A husband’s insistence that his wife must live alongside the woman with whom he is having an extramarital affair will amount to mental cruelty of the highest degree, the Jharkhand High Court recently observed while dissolving a marriage that had remained broken since 2019. A Division Bench of Justices Sujit Narayan Prasad and Pradeep Kumar Srivastava held that the husband compelling the wife to accept his affair with another woman under the guise of a "younger sister" shatters matrimonial trust irreparably. Hence, it allowed the appeal filed by the wife, a medical practitioner, challenging a November 2023 order of a family court at Hazaribagh which had dismissed her divorce petition filed under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The High Court held that the family court had appreciated the evidence in a piecemeal manner and overlooked the principle of preponderance of probabilities applicable to matrimonial proceedings. items.title: Why Poland wants a stronger relationship with India | The Hindu Editorial
items.summary: Why is Poland seeking a closer partnership with India? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s visit to India highlighted growing cooperation in trade, technology, defence, critical minerals, renewable energy and geopolitical coordination. With India and the European Union preparing to finalise a landmark Free Trade Agreement, Poland is positioning itself as a key European partner for New Delhi. This editorial explores what both countries stand to gain, the challenges that remain, and why the India-Poland relationship could become increasingly important in Europe’s engagement with India.
